0.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_000_001
0.description: If you would master Triple Triad, then you must first learn its rules. Is there aught you wish me to explain?

10.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_300_001
10.description: There are a number of advanced rules that can alter the way a Triple Triad match is played. Advanced rules can be applied under a variety of circumstances, and can be considered either “regional rules” or “match rules.”

16.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_Q3_000_001
16.description: Which rule will you ask about?

33.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_100_001
33.description: At its heart, Triple Triad is a battle between two opponents, wherein the clever composition and strategic use of a five-card deck mean the difference between victory and defeat.

34.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_100_002
34.description: The game can be transformed by its plethora of advanced rules, which force even experienced players to adapt and revise their seemingly invincible repertoires. Once you've mastered the basics, there's still so much left to learn!

35.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_001
35.description: The set of five cards you play during a match is known as a “deck.” Building a dependable deck from the cards that you've acquired is the first step towards defeating rival players!

36.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_002
36.description: You must <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Use<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> the cards in your inventory to register them to your <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Card List<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>. Your card list can be accessed via the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Gold Saucer<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> options found under <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Character<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> in the main menu.

37.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_003
37.description: Select <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Card Decks<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, also found under <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Gold Saucer<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, to build decks using your registered cards.

38.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_004
38.description: Each deck may only contain a limited number of cards with a <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>rarity<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> rating of four or more stars. A warning message will be displayed should you attempt to exceed the limit.

39.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_005
39.description: You can build and name up to five individual decks. Decks can also be created automatically by using the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Recommended<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> button.

40.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_200_006
40.description: Unwanted cards in your inventory─doubles of those already registered to your card list, for example─can be sold to the Triple Triad trader.

41.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_001
41.description: Ah, yes, where would we be without rules!? Simply put, Triple Triad is a game wherein two opponents seek to best one another through the medium of specially marked cards.

42.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_002
42.description: Each player holds a hand of five such cards, otherwise known as a “deck.” You can build several decks, but you'll need to pick the one you wish to play with before the match can begin.

43.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_003
43.description: Once the participants have selected their decks, the player to place the first card is chosen at random. The players continue to take turns placing cards until the match is decided at the end of nine turns.

44.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_004
44.description: Each turn consists of a player selecting a single card and placing it on an empty space on the playing grid. Pay close attention to the four numbers displayed on the card─each value corresponds to one of the card's four sides.

45.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_005
45.description: The numbers on a card can range from “1” to “9,” with “10” being represented by an “A” (read as “ace”).

46.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_105
46.description: You can “capture” your opponent's card by placing a card with a larger number on the adjacent side. The captured card's color will change, and it will now be counted towards your total.

47.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_006
47.description: Once the playing grid is full, whoever has control over the most cards─including the unplayed card in the second player's deck─is declared the winner.

48.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_301_007
48.description: The match result─victory, defeat, or draw─will determine your reward. If you wish, you can always challenge your opponent to a rematch. Developing a friendly rivalry can be one of the most enjoyable aspects of the game!

49.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_700_001
49.description: In Triple Triad matches, each player has an overall time limit of ninety seconds in which to decide their moves.

50.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_700_002
50.description: You will, however, have a five-second “thinking” window at the beginning of every turn, during which the turn timer will not deplete. But don't ponder for too long! Once this grace period ends, the timer will start ticking down again from wherever it left off.

51.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_700_003
51.description: Should the timer run down completely, you will only have the aforementioned five-second window to make each remaining move─failure to do so resulting in a card being chosen and placed for you. Needless to say, a wise player soon learns the importance of time management!

52.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_SYSTEM_700_004
52.description: The five-second thinking window is counted down on the turn timer, with this grace period being displayed on the gauge in red. Once this red section is depleted, the timer will immediately transition to counting down from the match-allotted ninety-second time limit.

53.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_302_002
53.description: The term “regional rules” is used to describe those advanced rules whose implementation varies by location or with the hour of the day.

54.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_302_003
54.description: This category of rules is updated daily at <hex:0206020103><hex:020821DBFF1D020919DB02030405060708090A0B0C0D02030405060708090A0B0C030D03> <hex:020810E0DB0DFF05702E6D2EFF05612E6D2E03> (Earth time). A maximum of two regional rules will be in effect at any one time, and each locale tends to favor certain rule sets.

55.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_303_002
55.description: The term “match rules” is used to describe those advanced rules that are decided by the participants.

56.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_303_003
56.description: A maximum of two match rules can be in effect at any one time, and are set automatically by NPC opponents. When challenging fellow player characters, however, you are given the decision as to which match rules will be in play.

57.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_401_001
57.description: “All Open” is a rule wherein all five cards in each deck are made visible to both players. Check your opponent's deck carefully before making a move!

58.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_402_001
58.description: “Three Open” is a rule wherein three random cards in each deck are made visible to both players. You'll just have to guess what surprises your rival has hidden behind the other two...

59.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_403_001
59.description: “Same” is a rule that adds a new condition to the capture mechanic. If the numbers of two or more cards are the same as the numbers on the adjacent sides of the card you place, you gain control of every matching card.

60.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_403_002
60.description: This rule also allows you to score a “Combo” capture. Should the cards you capture lie adjacent to “weaker” cards (i.e. cards with smaller numbers on the neighboring sides), those cards will fall under your control as well!

61.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_403_003
61.description: Only one of the two or more matching cards needs to belong to your opponent for the Same capture mechanic to take effect. Of all the advanced rules, this one is infamous for its tendency to invite sudden reversals of fortune!

62.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_404_001
62.description: When “Sudden Death” is in effect, any match that ends in a draw will be restarted from turn one.

63.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_404_002
63.description: Your deck for this new match will consist of the cards you had control over at the end of the previous game. But fear not! Your original cards will be returned to you upon the culmination of the Sudden Death match.

64.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_404_003
64.description: Sudden Death will continue until one player wins or until five more consecutive drawn matches have been played, at which point the game will result in a draw.

65.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_405_001
65.description: “Plus” is a rule that adds a new condition to the capture mechanic. If the numbers of two or more cards have the same total when added to the numbers on the adjacent sides of the card you place, you gain control of every matching card.

66.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_405_002
66.description: This rule also allows you to score a “Combo” capture. Should the cards you capture lie adjacent to “weaker” cards (i.e. cards with smaller numbers on the neighboring sides), those cards will fall under your control as well!

67.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_405_003
67.description: Only one of the two or more matching cards needs to belong to your opponent for the Plus capture mechanic to take effect. This rule can be especially dangerous for those who rely on uniformly powerful decks!

68.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_406_001
68.description: When the “Random” rule is in effect, your chosen deck will be replaced with five cards selected at random from your entire card list.

69.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_406_002
69.description: Though a healthy dose of luck can certainly play a part, your surest ally will be the ability to adapt and form a strategy with the cards you've been dealt. Consistently winning Random matches is the mark of a true Triple Triad master!

70.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_407_001
70.description: “Order” is a rule wherein you are required to play each card in the order that it appears in your deck. The position of your trump cards can claim─or cost─you victory.

71.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_408_001
71.description: “Chaos” is a rule wherein the card you play each turn is selected at random from your deck. Rise to the challenge, and you may just discover a new winning strategy!

72.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_409_001
72.description: With the “Reverse” rule in effect, the conditions for capturing cards are switched so that smaller numbers are more powerful than larger numbers. A Reverse match is probably not the best place to bring your legendary cards...

73.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_410_001
73.description: When the “Fallen Ace” rule is in effect, the all-powerful “A” becomes susceptible to capture by the lowly “1.”

74.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_410_002
74.description: If the Reverse rule is also in play, a “1” will then become vulnerable to capture by an “A.” Understanding the interplay of multiple rules can certainly be a daunting task!

75.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_411_001
75.description: “Ascension” is a rule that affects cards that are grouped into a specific type, such as “Primal” or “Society.”

76.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_411_002
76.description: When placed on the playing grid, the number values on these cards are increased by one for every card of that type that is in play.

77.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_411_003
77.description: Numbers that are increased to “11” or more are considered to be of “A” rank. This is an important point to consider if the Fallen Ace rule is also in effect!

78.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_412_001
78.description: “Descension” is a rule that affects cards that are grouped into a specific type, such as “Primal” or “Society.”

79.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_412_002
79.description: When placed on the playing grid, the number values on these cards are decreased by one for every card of that type that is in play.

80.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_412_003
80.description: Any number that is decreased to “0” or less is treated as a “1.”

81.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_413_001
81.description: When the “Swap” rule is in effect, one card from your deck is switched with one of your opponent's before the match begins. The cards to be swapped are chosen at random, and are returned to their original owners at the end of the game.

82.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_414_001
82.description: When the “Roulette” rule is in effect, the advanced rules for the match will be chosen at random.

83.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_414_002
83.description: This is the perfect choice for creating a level battlefield between rivals who excel with particular rule sets!

84.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_415_001
84.description: When the “Draft” rule is in effect, participants will not have access to their individual decks and must instead play using cards provided by the Gold Saucer.

85.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_415_002
85.description: Contests are usually fought with decks prepared carefully in advance, but a Draft match begins with each participant improvising a deck from a random selection of cards. Victory will hinge upon both shrewd card choice and a healthy dose of luck.

86.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_SYSTEM_415_003
86.description: Before the match begins, each participant must build a five-card deck from the random selection on offer. Novice players are encouraged to make use of the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Recommended<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> button.

87.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_500_001
87.description: Once you've built a deck and studied the rules, you're ready to seek battle against your fellow Triple Triad enthusiasts!

88.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_500_002
88.description: The game has gained an avid following, and you're sure to find willing participants in various locales across Eorzea.

89.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_500_003
89.description: Please be aware that, even outside the Gold Saucer, you will need to spend MGP to begin a Triple Triad match against anyone who is not a fellow adventurer. But in addition to earning you even more MGP, victory against far-flung opponents may possibly reward you with new and rare cards!

90.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_500_004
90.description: MGP is not required to begin a Triple Triad match between player characters. Such matches will also never feature cards as rewards─instead, a bonus amount of MGP is awarded upon victory. Bonus MGP can be earned a maximum of five times per day.

91.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_500_005
91.description: Matches between player characters must be played in sanctioned Triple Triad areas. Regulation playing areas are found not only in the Gold Saucer, but also in the various chapters of the Adventurers' Guild, outpost taverns, and other locations designated as sanctuaries.

92.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_600_001
92.description: What is the Battlehall, you ask? Why, none other than <hex:021A020203>the<hex:021A020103> destination for Triple Triad enthusiasts from across the realm who seek to try their hand against a worthy opponent. If you're looking for a rousing match, why not visit and see for yourself?

93.name: TEXT_CMNGSCTRIPLETRIADGUIDE_00238_TTGUIDE_600_002
93.description: You can enter the Triple Triad Battlehall by speaking with the Triple Triad master, or via the Duty Finder.
